title: What These Rules Are
key_points: These Rules are a book of order, not a technique for winning arguments.
They govern how a debate proceeds, not what either side says.
Built in three layers: Maxims at the base, Law over the text, Rules built on both.
A debate under order lets disagreement end in a settled decision instead of a quarrel.

verse.text: Let all things be done decently and in order.

scene.caption: Order, not a bag of tricks.
scene.alt: A quiet hall with pillars, a podium, and a stack of books standing in ordered light.

title: The Maxims
key_points: Four maxims ground every rule: equal weights, true-or-false statements, one truth, and rules from maxims.
A rule binding one side and not the other is a false weight and its verdict worthless.
Every statement either matches reality or it does not, regardless of either side's opinion.
Truth in one field cannot contradict truth in another, so points transfer across subjects.

verse.text: Divers weights, and divers measures, both of them are alike abomination to the LORD.

scene.caption: Equal weights for every side.
scene.alt: A pair of balanced scales standing on an open plain under a golden sky, resting on a stack of books.

title: The Law and the Rules
key_points: The Law fixes which copy of the Rules is official: the author's own last, complete, English version.
Nine written Rules cover equal time, agreed sub points, two objections, precedent, and unanimous boolean votes.
A disputed sub point tables the whole debate until it is settled as its own debate.
A debater cannot vote to let a point stand that he himself disagrees with.

verse.text: But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.

scene.caption: One official version, sealed.
scene.alt: A sealed scroll resting on a table beside a stack of books under a dusky sky.

title: Formats
key_points: A format only shapes how time and turns are divided; the Rules stay the same.
In the Small Group format, each side gets a matching, uninterrupted turn for everything it does.
Questions, evasions, and false answers are handled inside the speaker's own turn, not the other side's.
Any new format must still keep equal time and true-or-false decisions for both sides.

verse.text: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

scene.caption: Turns measured by equal time.
scene.alt: A podium and an hourglass standing side by side in a bright, pillared hall.

title: Settling a Point
key_points: Settling a point starts from the written transcript, pinned to the exact sentence spoken.
Both sides must agree on what a sentence means before it can be judged.
Both sides state in advance what would prove the point false, or it is not a boolean.
A point is won only by direct agreement or by logic both sides accepted beforehand.

verse.text: Can two walk together, except they be agreed?

scene.caption: Agree the logic; let it judge.
scene.alt: A scroll and a lamp beside a pair of scales at dawn, marking the point that agreement settles.
